summary: With the admin_ops_events write authority resting at supabase, the boundary Worker read authority was set to d1 for one deliberate read-only window (version 38b27a5b-ae1a-4d1d-94a1-49ee51236e7d; admin write supabase, admin read d1, heartbeat write/read supabase, OIDC allowed refs main + codex/m7-go-search). Before the probe both stores held 412 admin_ops_events rows and the latest 20 IDs/order matched. The OIDC-authenticated GET /v1/ops/admin-events/list?limit=20 then returned the same 20 newest rows as the canonical Supabase listAdminOpsEvents(20): boundaryCount 20, supabaseCount 20, boundaryVsSupabase.holds true, differences [], ok true (directD1 disabled in GitHub). Because the boundary read authority was d1, boundary-vs-Supabase is itself a D1 projection comparison. Cloudflare Observability recorded exactly one authenticated GET (200/outcome ok, wallTimeMs 471, auth-failure count 0) on version 38b27a5b and no writes. After the run Supabase and D1 counts both stayed 412 and the Supabase watchdog run_id stayed the prior 36377461933, proving no heartbeat/watchdog/admin-event write. The Worker was restored to resting version bc257622-da6e-45fb-9be3-46d9c0e56991 (admin write/read supabase, no temporary allowed-refs binding) and unauthenticated list GET returns 401. This marks M11.4R LIVE-READ-PARITY-PASS; it does NOT claim a combined full-d1 admin_ops_events read/write cutover or global M11 completion.
